identity_and_auth.user_identity_model: Account is required; identity is OpenAI-managed. Two sign-in contracts: (1) 'Sign in with ChatGPT' (OAuth browser flow that returns an access token) which ties usage to the user's ChatGPT plan (Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, Enterprise) and inherits the ChatGPT workspace's permissions, RBAC, and Enterprise retention/residency settings; (2) API key sign-in, which bills through the OpenAI Platform at usage-based rates and follows the API org's data settings. Enterprise workspaces additionally support Codex access tokens (created by permitted members) that represent the workspace user for non-interactive/trusted automation, and device-code auth (`codex login --device-auth`). MFA is recommended; SSO/social login (Google/Microsoft/Apple) supported via the ChatGPT account layer.
identity_and_auth.multi_user_collaboration: Org/team collaboration is layered on ChatGPT workspaces. Enterprise/Business workspaces provide RBAC, admin permissions (Workspace Settings > Permissions & roles), governance data tied to access-token identity, and shared environment caches across all users with access to a cloud environment. 'Team Config' lets teams share defaults, rules, and skills checked into the repo's `.codex` directory, auto-applied when a user opens that repo. OpenAI has hinted at (but not fully shipped) collaborative sharing of agent threads across team members. [uncertain] Direct real-time co-editing of a single thread by multiple users is not described.

workspace_model.workspace_definition: Multi-layered. In the Codex macOS app the top-level organizing unit is a 'project'; inside each project a user creates 'threads', where each thread is one agent instance. A project maps to a local Git repository/directory. For Codex Cloud, the unit is a 'cloud environment' that is bound to a GitHub repository and is configured with a base image (codex-universal), setup/maintenance scripts, env vars, and secrets. So 'workspace' is not a single concept: locally it is a directory/Git repo (project), and in the cloud it is an environment record bound to a repo. The term 'workspace' in the ChatGPT-Enterprise sense (governance/identity) is distinct from the Codex project/environment.
workspace_model.workspace_session_binding: Sessions (threads) are scoped to a project, and each thread is an independent agent instance with its own preserved conversation history. A user can have multiple active threads per project simultaneously (multi-tasking is a core design goal), and each thread independently selects an execution mode (Local, Worktree, or Cloud). Session history is also shared across surfaces: the app picks up session history and configuration from the Codex CLI and IDE extension, so threads/Auto Context can be continued across app/IDE/CLI. CLI sessions are bound to a working directory by default (resume shows sessions in the cwd; `--all` shows all).
workspace_model.context_scoping: Context is layered: workspace/repo-level via AGENTS.md files (repeated instructions live here) and Team Config under `.codex`; session/thread-level via the conversation history and Auto Context that can be shared across app and IDE; global/account-level via plan limits and user config (CODEX_HOME, ~/.codex/config). Cloud-environment-level context includes the base image, installed dependencies, env vars, and secrets bound to that environment. Workspace instruction loading resolves the correct AGENTS.md even for remote/symlinked workspaces.
workspace_model.config_file_instruction_precedence: Primary instruction file is AGENTS.md (the cross-tool, OpenAI-promoted standard) discovered per-repo and per-directory; nested AGENTS.md files apply to their subtree. Team Config lives under the `.codex` directory in a repo and is auto-loaded when the repo is opened. User/global config lives at ~/.codex/config (TOML) and CODEX_HOME. Cloud-environment config (setup script, maintenance script, env vars, secrets) is stored in the environment record. [uncertain] Exact precedence ordering/cascade between AGENTS.md, Team Config, and user config, and any max-file-size cap on AGENTS.md, are not explicitly documented in sources reviewed.
workspace_model.source_corpus_grounding_scope: Not applicable. Codex is a software-engineering agent grounded in a Git repository/codebase, not a curated source/corpus (no NotebookLM/Perplexity-Space style bounded source set). The 'corpus' is effectively the repo contents plus pre-installed dependencies; during the agent phase the agent is restricted to repo code and dependencies (no external web).

persistence_and_history.persistence_mechanism: Hybrid. Local CLI/app: a 'Rollout System' persists all session events as append-only JSONL files under ~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/ (rollout-*.jsonl) and indexes them in a local SQLite database for retrieval and state restore; a separate ~/.codex/history.jsonl holds local transcript history (cappable via history.max_bytes). Cloud: state lives in OpenAI-managed cloud infrastructure; cloud environments cache resulting container state after the setup script runs (shared across workspace users for Business/Enterprise). Append-only event-log model for transcripts; container state is snapshot/cache based.
persistence_and_history.session_history: CLI/app sessions are stored as rollout-*.jsonl files (one per session) containing the full conversation, tool calls, and token usage, auto-saved (saving is always on), indexed in SQLite. Session IDs are auto-generated; files cannot be manually renamed for resume purposes (resume relies on the session_id inside the JSONL). History is browsable via a picker (`codex resume`, `--last`, `--all`, `<SESSION_ID>`) and via the app UI organized by project/thread. Exportable/portable by reading the JSONL directly (e.g., with jq). Known issue: unbounded logging/compaction history can bloat session files to hundreds of MB to GB. Cloud session history is browsable in the Codex web/app UI and shared across CLI/IDE/app surfaces.
persistence_and_history.memory_layering: Short-term/thread state = the per-thread rollout JSONL transcript (ephemeral within a session, persisted to disk). Durable cross-session instruction layer = user-authored AGENTS.md and Team Config (durable, repo-scoped). There is no described auto-generated/auto-summarized long-term 'memory' store akin to Windsurf/Claude auto-memory in the sources reviewed; durability comes from explicit instruction files plus resumable transcripts. Auto Context (working context shared across app/IDE) acts as a bridge between active threads. [uncertain] Existence of an automatic semantic long-term memory.
persistence_and_history.search_retrieval_history: Past sessions are retrievable: `codex resume` provides a picker of recent interactive sessions (cwd-scoped by default, `--all` for global); CLI v0.135 added history search. The SQLite index enables efficient retrieval/state restoration. A prior session can be reopened (resume) or branched (`/fork`) without manual copy-paste. [uncertain] Whether retrieval is full-text/semantic search over transcript content versus session-metadata picker is not fully specified (history search exists but its matching mode is unclear).
persistence_and_history.lifecycle_ttl_cleanup: Local transcripts are persistent by default and accumulate (no automatic TTL; can be capped by history.max_bytes, with oldest entries dropped and the file compacted when the cap is exceeded). Cloud environment container state is cached and persists until invalidated; the cache is automatically invalidated when the setup/maintenance script, env vars, or secrets change, or via a manual 'Reset cache'. Secrets are decrypted only for task execution and removed before the agent phase begins. [uncertain] Explicit TTL/expiration for cloud task containers and retention windows for cloud session history (these follow ChatGPT Enterprise retention settings when ChatGPT sign-in is used).

execution_and_isolation.sandbox_isolation_model: Cloud: each task runs in its own isolated, OpenAI-managed container (Ubuntu 24.04-based codex-universal base image), preventing access to the host or unrelated data; all outbound traffic passes through an HTTP/HTTPS proxy. Two-phase runtime: a setup phase WITH network access (to install deps via setup script), then an agent phase that is OFFLINE/network-OFF by default (configurable to limited or unrestricted). Local: an OS-enforced sandbox limits writes (typically to the workspace) plus an approval policy; sandbox mode + approval policy are independently configurable by risk tolerance. In nested Docker, the namespace/seccomp sandbox may be bypassed with `--sandbox danger-full-access`. Multiple cloud tasks run in parallel, each in its own sandbox.
execution_and_isolation.snapshot_state_restore: Yes — environment/machine state is captured independently of conversation history. Codex runs the setup script and caches the resulting container state; an optional maintenance script refreshes a resumed cached container (useful when the cached state ran on an older commit). Shell-environment snapshotting speeds up repeated commands (stable, on by default). Caches are shared across users for Business/Enterprise and are auto-invalidated on config/secret/script changes or manual reset. This filesystem/dependency snapshot is distinct from the JSONL session transcript.
execution_and_isolation.cloud_local_handoff: Strong cloud/local handoff. A thread can run in Local, Worktree, or Cloud mode; cloud task results can be applied locally ('local apply' pulls cloud results into the local repo) and cloud creates PRs. Session history and configuration are shared across CLI, IDE extension, app, and cloud, so a user can move between surfaces. Self-hosting is not supported (cloud runs only in OpenAI-managed infra); the CLI/local sandbox runs on the user's own machine.
execution_and_isolation.parallelism_subagent_fanout: First-class parallelism. The app manages many agents at once, one thread per agent, organized by project; multiple cloud tasks run simultaneously, each in its own sandbox. Git worktrees are the local parallelism primitive — each worktree is an isolated checkout (own branch, own Codex session) so multiple agents work the same repo without file conflicts. Spawned subagents each work in their own isolated environment (often an auto-created git worktree) and, as of v0.115.0 (Mar 2026), reliably inherit the parent's sandbox/network rules and profile layering, making subagent-driven parallel execution stable. Thread coordination (find/continue/pin/archive related threads, explicit background threads) is supported for local projects and worktrees.
execution_and_isolation.trigger_surface: Sessions are initiated from: the Codex macOS app, the CLI (interactive and headless), IDE extensions, and Codex web/cloud. Cloud tasks run asynchronously and can open PRs. API key / access tokens enable programmatic/CI/scheduler triggers. OpenAI has signaled a future 'automation cloud' for trigger-based jobs (e.g., on GitHub push). [uncertain] First-class Slack/GitHub-issue-mention triggers comparable to Copilot's issue assignment.

implementation.implementation_stack: Auth: OAuth (Sign in with ChatGPT), API keys, and Enterprise access tokens; identity layered on ChatGPT workspaces (RBAC, retention). Local session storage: append-only JSONL rollout files (~/.codex/sessions/.../rollout-*.jsonl) plus ~/.codex/history.jsonl, indexed by a local SQLite database (the 'Rollout System'). Config: TOML user config under ~/.codex (CODEX_HOME); AGENTS.md instruction files; Team Config under repo `.codex`. Cloud: OpenAI-managed isolated containers from the open-source codex-universal Ubuntu 24.04 image, container-state caching/snapshotting, an outbound HTTP/HTTPS proxy, encrypted secrets store (decrypted only at task time, removed before agent phase), and env-var injection. Cloud models: codex-1 (o3-derived) family. [uncertain] The specific cloud-side databases (e.g., Postgres/Mongo/Redis) backing cloud session history and environment metadata are not publicly documented.
implementation.applicability_to_labmate: Codex's two-layer model maps cleanly to Labmate's stack. (1) Session/thread = a unit Labmate can model as a LangGraph thread_id with append-only event persistence; Codex's append-only JSONL rollout + SQLite index is conceptually identical to Labmate's Redis Streams (active state, TTL) + MongoDB (durable session docs) split — adopt append-only event logs as the source of truth and a separate index for retrieval. (2) workspace_id scoping: emulate Codex's project>thread hierarchy — Labmate could scope sessions under a workspace_id (project) and allow N concurrent threads per workspace, with a Discord channel/thread acting as the trigger surface analogous to Codex's app threads. (3) Identity: Codex's 'identity inherits the org workspace's RBAC/retention' is a good model — bind Labmate user identity to the connector (Discord) account but allow an org/workspace overlay for shared rules. (4) Instruction layering: adopt an AGENTS.md-style repo/workspace-scoped instruction file plus a global/user layer, mirroring Codex AGENTS.md + Team Config + ~/.codex config. (5) Execution isolation: Codex's network-off-by-default agent phase with a separate network-on setup phase is a strong security default Labmate should mirror for any tool-execution sandbox, plus snapshot/cache of environment state independent of conversation history so a workspace's prepared env can be restored without replaying history.
